concepts.def: How close a value is to the true value
How close repeats are to each other
Same result with different person or kit

walkthroughs.body_html:
Identify the three variable types.

Independent → x-axis. Dependent → y-axis. Controls keep other things equal so the change in x is the only cause.

Accurate = close to true value. Precise = close repeats.

You can be precise but not accurate (a stuck clock is precise but wrong) or accurate but not precise (lucky guess once).

Gateway practicals include: enzyme rate (amylase + starch), osmosis (potato chips), food tests (Benedict's, biuret, iodine), microscope work.

Always cite the method and risk assessment.

mcqs.q: The variable you change is the:
Why is the secondary immune response to a pathogen faster and stronger than the primary?
options: Competition means physically fighting and is rare in nature.
The body produces a different, more powerful antibody during the secondary response.
Memory cells generated during the primary response can rapidly proliferate and produce large amounts of specific antibody on re-exposure.
The pathogen becomes weaker after the primary exposure, so the body has an easier job.

mcqs.q: What does it mean for an allele to be 'dominant'?
options: A dominant allele is the most common allele in a population.
Competition means physically fighting and is rare in nature.
A dominant allele physically destroys the recessive allele in the genome.
It is expressed in the phenotype when at least one copy is present (in a heterozygote).

mcqs.q: Why is interspecific competition between similar species important?
options: The body produces a different, more powerful antibody during the secondary response.
Two species cannot occupy exactly the same niche indefinitely — competition often leads to displacement or niche divergence.
Competition means physically fighting and is rare in nature.
Competition only happens between predators and their prey.

mcqs.q: A student changes the temperature of a reaction and measures the time taken. Which is the independent variable?
Three repeat readings are 4.8 s, 5.0 s and 5.2 s. What is the mean, and what does the closeness of the repeats suggest?
A student gets a reading of 9.9 cm³ when the true value is known to be 10.0 cm³. This reading is best described as:
Why does a student repeat an experiment several times and calculate a mean?
options: To reduce the effect of random error and identify anomalies
To change the independent variable each time
To make the experiment take longer
To guarantee a perfect single result
